transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Well, I came in because I just keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical. It's constant. I'll think I left a wrong number in a data release at work, or that I left the back door unlocked, or paid a bill from the wrong account. 

And the thing is, even when I know I checked it... my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some kind of disaster. It's just getting to be too much.
When these thoughts happen, do you feel compelled to repeatedly check things or perform specific actions to ease your anxiety?

Yes, I do. To try and calm myself down, I end up... well, reopening the spreadsheets I was working on. I'll reread emails line by line. Or I'll check the locks and the payment confirmations over and over again. 

I actually have to do it in a very specific, set order until it finally feels safe to me. It takes up so much time that some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, just checking, with nothing actually finished.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirmed classic compulsive checking rituals performed in a rigid order to neutralize intrusive, catastrophic doubts, taking hours each day. This rules out generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1) and major depressive disorder (F32) as primary causes.
